summary: Each piece is gated off at shapes where another piece runs, except sliding decode_1, and all three were built on master's exact submission blob (cc466fce), so their single runs already serve as per-piece controls. Projected headline is ~1.177 (T=1 pieces only) to ~1.181 (with paired). That is credible but sits inside the best's CI, so the readable signal is per-shape: sliding decode_1 should reach ~1.27x and full decode_1 ~1.20x.
justification: Base check: hyp branches sliding-fused-triton-decode1-port, paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton and bf16-shape-gated-triton-gemms-small-t all fork from a commit whose muse_decode_layer/submission.py blob is cc466fce, the same as master (post-expert-norm-triton-small-t, BEST job a017e10aec544c55). Their archived per-shape speedups (paired vs SGLang in the same run) can therefore be compared directly with master's two runs (a017e10a submit 1.1665, 9dcaec31 check 1.1635), and those two runs agree per shape to within 1.4%. Per-shape deltas vs the master geomean: port, sliding decode_1 +3.85% (profile total 149.2 -> 141.1 us: FA3 10.2 + combine 3.6 + qk-norm/cast/store/norm-gate glue replaced by _sliding_fused_kernel 13.7 us); GEMMs at T=1, sliding decode_1 +3.6% and full decode_1 +3.5% (cuBLAS nvjet qkv+pooler 32.6 + o 7.2 + unpool 5.1 + splitKreduce 5.0 = ~50 us of kernel time -> Triton 25.3 + 13.7 + 6.5 = ~45.5 us; profile total 149.2 -> 144.5). The two sliding decode_1 changes replace disjoint kernels (GEMMs vs the attention chain between them), so their savings should add. If anything the sum is slightly conservative, because each piece separately paid for losing cuBLAS/PDL overlap at the qkv->attention and attention->o boundaries, and stacked those boundaries are paid once. Additive model: sliding decode_1 1.178 -> ~1.27x (yours ~134-135 us), full decode_1 1.164 -> ~1.205x. Plugging those plus the paired run's full batch>1 rows into the TASK.md scoring (per-load weighted sums, geomean over 6 loads, SGLang times from master): restack with T=1 pieces only = 1.1774, with paired on all four full batch>1 shapes = 1.1813, master modelled = 1.165. The stated ~1.18 is credible. Almost all of the gain (~+1.0%) is the decode_1 load. Gating to tokens == 1 is right on the data. The original T<=16 gate hit decode_1 (T=1), verify_1 (T=8) and decode_16 (T=16), and those rows were +3.6/+3.5, -4.0/-3.4 and -4.1/-2.2 respectively, consistent across both layers. Scored T are only {1, 8, 16, 32, 128, 256}, so ==1 is equivalent to any gate below 8. The gains the GEMM run shows at T=32/128 (full decode_32 +8.2%, full verify_16 +3.2%) are on shapes where its code never runs, so they are noise; full decode_32 has bimodal per-rep ratios (1.12 vs 1.36) in master too. WEAKEST LINK: the paired pad/unpad piece. Its rows (full decode_16 +2.0%, decode_32 +1.0%, verify_16 +3.1%, verify_32 -0.4%) are no larger than the spread on untouched shapes in sibling runs (port run sliding verify_16 -2.5%, sliding verify_32 +2.2%; GEMM run full verify_16 +3.2% with no code active). It is worth ~+0.35% on the headline and cannot be attributed from one run. A second weak link is the headline itself: +1.0-1.3% over 1.1665 sits inside the best's CI [1.149, 1.184] and inside the run's own >= +/-1.5% interval, so a headline-only classifier will likely call it within-ci/unproven again even if every piece works. Judge it on the sliding decode_1 and full decode_1 rows. The `expected` list is incomplete. It omits full decode_1 faster (T=1 GEMMs, ~+3.5%), the largest-weight full-layer move, and full verify_16 faster (paired), the only shape FINDINGS credits the paired piece with. 'verify_1 flat' is right relative to master, not relative to the GEMM run.
confounders: landed list is empty for this problem's lineage tracking, but master already carries post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (SMALL_T_POST_NORM path, _post_norm_combine_kernel at small T): all three pieces were measured on that exact blob (cc466fce), so it is a shared base, not a confounder.

Within the restack, sliding decode_1 is the only shape where two pieces both run (sliding port + T=1 GEMMs). They replace disjoint kernels and the qkv tensor the fused kernel reads is the same contiguous [1, 2304] bf16 output either way (fused kernel takes qkv.stride(0); Triton qkv GEMM writes contiguously). Expect additivity, measured by sliding decode_1 vs ~1.27x.

paired pad/unpad is gated window == 0 and batch > 1, so it never runs on a shape where the port (sliding, batch 1, q_len 1) or the T==1 GEMMs run: no runtime interaction. Its _paired_norm_gate_kernel reads the gate from qkv with qkv.stride(0) and assumes unit inner stride. That holds on master's _gemm path, which is the only path it sees at batch > 1.
interference: No companion warranted. The three pieces' own runs on the identical base blob already isolate each sub-change: port alone (12198572363b49a4), paired alone (a92b64be4c6547d3), and GEMMs alone at T<=16 (6076ae1f250143aa, whose T=1 rows are the T==1-gate control). The restack's result decomposes by shape. Sliding decode_1 tests additivity of port + GEMMs against two measured singles. Full decode_1 should reproduce the GEMM run's +3.5%. Full batch>1 should reproduce the paired run. verify_1 and decode_16 should return to master (confirming the gate). A further control would only re-measure code already measured, and identical code returns its cached result anyway. The paired piece's ambiguity is noise, not interference: a companion cannot fix it; only stacking a larger full-layer change on top can.
rules_flags: None blocking; all three pieces passed 13/13 with checks.ok and no flags on this base.

Port: _COUNTERS (module-level ticket counters zeroed on first eager call, self-resetting) and _inv_freq hold no input-derived data, which is OK. The kernel attends to the whole 2,048-token window (WINDOW=cfg['window']), and its gate reads config only.

GEMMs: _FALLBACK_SEEN prints host-side shapes only (no tensor values) and gating is on token count and shapes, which is OK. When narrowing to tokens == 1, keep the routing a pure config/shape predicate (e.g. small_t = tokens == 1). The unpooler slice path is still taken only at T<=8, which T==1 satisfies.

Hand-merge risk: the port re-indents the entire attention block under `else:` and paired rewrites lines inside that block. The paired edits (_pair_pad_q_kernel replacing the torch.zeros + slice copies, and the `if paired: ... else: o_norm_gate` epilogue) must land inside the else branch, and `o` must stay defined on all three routes (sliding-b1 fused, paired, plain). Self-review the merged kernel_fn: a mismerge here would make the result useless and could fail correctness.
open_questions: Why did the Triton GEMMs lose wall time at T=8/16 while their kernel sums were lower? Candidates: lost PDL overlap between cuBLAS and the next sglang kernel, or the 128-CTA Triton pooler starving the side-stream router that overlaps it. The same mechanism is present at T=1 and is netted into the +3.5%. If it is the router overlap, a T=1 restack is unaffected; if it is PDL, the stacked Triton->Triton chain at sliding decode_1 might be slightly super-additive.

If the headline lands inside the CI (likely, ~1.177-1.181 vs best 1.1665 [1.149, 1.184]), should promotion use the per-shape decode_1 rows (expected well outside noise: sliding ~+7.5%, full ~+3.5%) rather than the headline? That decision belongs to the harvester.

Should the T=1 GEMM warmup in _prepare_small_t_gemms be trimmed to m=1 now that only T==1 routes to it? It is harmless as is (untimed prepare), but leaving the 1..16 workspaces makes the code claim more than it uses.
